remaining_gaps: Clause 1 (the Tariff Schedules of the United States amendments to apply to articles entered on and after January 1, 1967) cannot be decided from held sources: the held 19 U.S.C. 2051 note, 75 FR 69583 and 76 FR 51914 say only that the duty-free treatment is now at HTSUS subheading 9817.00.40. Missing: the statute and effective date by which the Harmonized Tariff Schedule replaced the Tariff Schedules of the United States, and the text of HTSUS subheading 9817.00.40 with its U.S. notes.

Clause 2 designates the United States Information Agency, which was abolished by Pub. L. 105-277 div. G title XIII with its functions transferred to the Department of State; the held 19 U.S.C. 2051 note only cross-refers to 22 U.S.C. 6531, 6532 and 6551. Missing: the text of 22 U.S.C. 6531, 6532 and 6551 (abolition date, transfer of functions and treatment of references) so the successor designation and its date can be quoted; the held 22 CFR part 61 and the 2010 CBP rule describe State administering the Agreement but are not that statute.

EO 14207 (90 FR 9583, effective February 10, 2025), section 2(b), revokes any applicable provisions of Executive Order 11348 in the course of eliminating the Federal Executive Institute but does not name which provisions are meant; the text of EO 11348 never mentions the Federal Executive Institute, and the interagency training clauses (sections 202(d), 302(c) and 302(e)) are the only candidates. Missing: an OPM or White House record identifying the provisions of EO 11348 treated as revoked by EO 14207 section 2(b), so each of the 40 inventory clauses can be classified as operative or terminated on 2025-02-10.

The dossier inventory also contains two fragments that are not clauses (EO:11348#sec202-a-dup2, the reference to section 4102(a) inside section 202(e), and EO:11348#sec402-6) and would need an absolute-span inventory correction; the held 5 U.S.C. 4103 note extract holds only the preamble of the order, so no held current-law text prints the clauses.

Section 1 designates the Department of State as the Central Authority under the Hague Service Convention, but the held 28 CFR 0.49(b) (2025 edition) assigns the Central Authority functions under that Convention to the Civil Division of the Department of Justice. Section 3 of the order lets the Secretary of State, with the Attorney General's concurrence for Justice designations, modify the designations. Missing: the dated instrument that modified or displaced the section 1 (and section 2) designations, and the amendment history (source line and date) of 28 CFR 0.49(b); only the 2025 edition of 28 CFR 0.49 is held, so no first-end date, actor or mechanism can be quoted, and no held current-law text shows sections 2 and 3 still operative.

The order has 22 sections (40 inventory clauses) that must each be placed against 5 U.S.C. chapter 71 (Civil Service Reform Act of 1978, Pub. L. 95-454, title VII, effective January 11, 1979) and EO 12107 section 2-301, which amended the order effective January 1, 1979. Held: 5 U.S.C. 7101, 7103 and 7135 only; section 7135(b) preserves policies, regulations, procedures and decisions established under EO 11491 but does not say the order's own commands continue. Missing: the text of 5 U.S.C. 7102-7134 and the title VII effective-date provisions (Pub. L. 95-454 section 907), and a source stating the disposition of EO 11491 itself (the held 5 U.S.C. 7101 note extract contains only the heading, amendment list and preamble). Also missing: the unnamed 1971 memoranda cited in the OFR catalog and EO 12107's full text-level effect on each section. Held evidence therefore does not show EO 11491 in force on 2026-10-14 clause by clause, and no YES claim is supported.

Section 1(a) permits veterans readjustment appointments only to positions up to GS-5 for Vietnam-era veterans with not more than fourteen years of education, while the held 5 CFR 307.103 and 307.102 (current part 307, which still cites EO 11521 as authority) allow appointments up to GS-11 for covered veterans under 38 U.S.C. 4214; section 4(b) limits the Vietnam era, and sections 1(b), 1(f), 2 and 5 refer to the Civil Service Commission and its guidelines. Missing: dated sources showing which instrument (Pub. L. 93-508 section 402 and later amendments of 38 U.S.C. 4214, or earlier editions of 5 CFR part 307) displaced or amended each of the 21 inventory clauses, with quoted text, so each clause can be classified as operative or terminated with an exact first-end date.

EO 12107 section 2-101(b) substitutes Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission in the order (effective January 1, 1979), which would be a later event on the affected clauses, but no clause-level end evidence is held for the substantive conflicts above.
